primary_meaning: Assurance/hope of salvation that protects the believer’s mind (thoughts, confidence, and resolve) against doubt, despair, and spiritual attack, as a piece of the Armor of God

alternatives.meaning: Specifically the ‘hope of salvation’ (future-oriented confidence in deliverance) rather than present assurance of salvation already received
basis: eschatological emphasis in some Protestant and evangelical expositions

alternatives.meaning: Christ’s own salvific work or divine warrior imagery applied to the believer (God’s helmet transferred to the Christian)
General readiness or sobriety of the Christian soldier without special emphasis on mental protection

notes: Virtually all mainstream Christian traditions (patristic, medieval, Reformation, modern evangelical/Catholic) treat the phrase as part of the Ephesians 6 spiritual-armor catalogue and link it to mental/spiritual protection via salvation; the main variation is only whether the accent falls on present assurance or future hope.
